plan.title: Planetary gearsets: one gearset, many ratios

objectives.statement: Identify the sun, the planets, the carrier and the ring of a planetary gearset, and state which members can be the input, the output or the held member.
objectives.criterion: Correct identification on an assembly description

objectives.statement: Calculate the output speed and direction of a simple planetary gearset from the tooth counts, the held member and the input speed, with the Willis equation.
Choose the held member and the input that meet a speed and direction requirement, and justify the choice with the resulting ratio.
objectives.criterion: 3 lab requirements out of 3 met, and the hoist drive configured correctly

items.title: One gearset, many ratios
items.description: Hook: the same compact gearset reduces speed, increases it or reverses it, depending on which member is held. Applications: automatic transmissions, wind turbines, electric drives.

lockedTexts.text: A planetary gearset fits in the space of a single gear, yet it can **reduce** speed, **increase** it or **reverse** it. Automatic transmissions, wind turbines and compact electric drives all rely on it. What decides the ratio is not the gears you buy: it is **which member you hold**.

items.title: Anatomy and the Willis equation
items.description: The four members and their tooth counts (30-tooth sun, 24-tooth planets, 78-tooth ring). The configuration rule and the Willis equation, then a worked example with the ring held.

lockedTexts.text:
**Hold one member, drive another, take the output from the third.** Whatever the configuration, the speeds obey the Willis equation:

$$Z_s\,n_s + Z_r\,n_r = (Z_s + Z_r)\,n_c$$

$Z$ is a number of teeth and $n$ a speed in rpm, negative when the member turns the other way; $s$, $r$ and $c$ stand for sun, ring and carrier. A held member has a speed of zero.

items.title: Your turn: sun held
items.description: Unscored practice question right after the worked example: same gearset, sun held, ring driven at 1,000 rpm; two attempts.

items.title: Gearbox lab
items.description: 3D test bench of the 30/78 gearset. Three requirements in a row (3.6:1 reduction, 3.6 times speed-up, reverse at 2.6:1). The learner chooses the held member and the input, runs the bench and reads the output speed. Scored.

items.title: Design decision: the hoist drive
items.description: Transfer to another gearset (24-tooth sun, 72-tooth ring): a 1,450 rpm motor must turn a hoist drum at about 360 rpm in the lifting direction. Three configurations, consequences shown as test bench results. Scored.

questions.stem: You open the cover of a planetary stage. Three small gears turn on pins, and the pins are fixed to a plate. Which member is that plate?

options.feedback: Right: the carrier holds the planet pins. When it turns, the planets orbit around the sun.
The sun is the toothed gear at the centre: the planets mesh with it, they are not mounted on it.
The ring is the outer gear with internal teeth: the planets mesh inside it, they are not mounted on it.

questions.stem: A planetary stage has a 20-tooth sun and a 60-tooth ring. The ring is held and the sun is driven at 2,000 rpm. At what speed does the carrier turn? Give a negative value if it turns the other way.

feedback.correct: Right: $20 \times 2000 + 60 \times 0 = 80\,n_c$, so $n_c = 500$ rpm, positive: same direction as the sun. The ratio is $1 + 60/20 = 4$.
feedback.incorrect: Write the Willis equation with $n_r = 0$: $Z_s\,n_s = (Z_s + Z_r)\,n_c$, then solve for $n_c$.

misconceptions.feedback: $2000 \times 20/60$ treats the sun and the ring as a fixed-axis pair. With the ring held, the carrier moves too, so the ratio is $1 + 60/20 = 4$.
The output only reverses when the carrier is held. Here the ring is held and the carrier is the output: $20 \times 2000 = 80\,n_c$.
You multiplied by the ratio instead of dividing: with the ring held, the carrier is the slowest member.

questions.stem: A machine needs an output that turns **faster** than its input and **in the same direction**. Which configurations of a simple planetary gearset meet this requirement? Select every correct answer.

options.text: Sun held, carrier driven, output on the ring
options.feedback: This one meets it: nr = (Zs + Zr)/Zr × nc, a factor above 1 with a positive sign. It is a mild overdrive.

options.text: Ring held, carrier driven, output on the sun
options.feedback: This one meets it: ns = (Zs + Zr)/Zs × nc, a large factor with a positive sign. It is the speed-up stage of many wind turbines.

options.text: Ring held, sun driven, output on the carrier
options.feedback: This is the strongest reduction: nc = Zs/(Zs + Zr) × ns, slower than the input.

options.text: Carrier held, ring driven, output on the sun
options.feedback: The sun does turn faster, but the minus sign in ns = −(Zr/Zs) × nr means it turns the other way.
